Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-26
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (CSM), Luca (Redwood SE); Dana, Ethan, Maya, Alex (Pegasus)

Summary (auto): quick alignment on kickoff scope; many security questions; pilot to run on Dedicated but exploring Private for data residency.

00:00 Jordan Meyers: Hey everyone, thanks for joining -- Jordan from Redwood. I think we have the right folks for a kickoff, quick round of intros?
00:14 Dana Ortiz: Hi I'm Dana, head of ML at Pegasus. We'll be owning the model integration and evaluation.
00:19 Ethan Park: Ethan, platform lead, I'll handle networking and infra.
00:22 Maya Lin: Maya, security. We'll be the gate for compliance docs.
00:25 Alex Chen: Alex, SRE, on-call for production.
00:28 Jordan Meyers: Great. Samira do you want to set expectations for the call?
00:31 Samira Gupta: Yeah, thanks. We want to align on pilot scope, timeline, what resources each side needs; outline the onboarding runbook and get next steps. Should be pretty light, mostly intake.
00:45 Luca Romano: Quick note -- from an SE perspective, we'll propose a dev Dedicated pool to start, that tends to be fastest for iteration. Private can come later if you need VPC/on-prem.
00:57 Ethan Park: When you say Dedicated, is that fully isolated GPU pool in your cloud? We need to know about VPC peering or egress rules.
01:05 Luca Romano: It's tenant-isolated compute, yes. For network we do two options: peering (VPC-to-VPC) or customer-managed NAT for outbound. Peering preferred for lower latency, but requires routing approval.
01:18 Maya Lin: We need details about encryption at rest, KMS integration and where logs live. SOC2 evidence would be great to review.
01:25 Jordan Meyers: Totally, we'll share SOC2, our SAML SSO guide, and KMS integration notes. I'll drop links in the follow-up.
01:33 Dana Ortiz: For pilot success, we care about 95th percentile latency under 400ms for short chat-style queries and throughput around 500-1k QPS peak. Is that reasonable?
01:44 Luca Romano: 400ms 95th is ambitious on large models if not batched; with prefix caching and continuous batching we can usually get there for smaller seq lengths. If you quantize model or use a distilled variant it's easier.
01:58 Ethan Park: How does Redwood handle fallbacks if Dedicated capacity spikes? We have seasonal traffic and can't have timeouts.
02:06 Samira Gupta: We support routing policies and automatic fallback to hosted lower-tier models; for critical flows we recommend canarying and setting fallback to a cost-tier model to preserve availability. We'll include recommended policies in the runbook.
02:24 Alex Chen: Are there limits on KV cache sizes or session stickiness? Our chat sessions rely on long context sometimes.
02:31 Luca Romano: KV cache is managed by the runtime; session stickiness is supported via session tokens. For long-horizon contexts we recommend progressive summarization to keep cost down. We'll add the config knobs.
02:50 Maya Lin: On logging: what are the retention windows? We need audit logs for at least 12 months for compliance.
02:58 Jordan Meyers: Our enterprise package can store audit logs for 12+ months; default hosted retention is shorter but Dedicated/Private customers can extend retention. We'll flag pricing add-on.
03:12 Dana Ortiz: Ok, for the initial pilot we plan to ingest 3 months of historical prompts to create eval sets, then run the pilot against production traffic with masked PII. We'll need guidance on data handling.
03:25 Samira Gupta: We'll share a data handling checklist — PII masking, retention, and KMS ops. Also a quick note: if you plan on on-prem deployment later, there are additional packaging steps.
03:40 Ethan Park: Network-wise, our security team wants to avoid opening inbound ports; peering is fine but requires the cloud ops review. How disruptive is peering?
03:51 Luca Romano: It requires a standard peering request plus some routing rules. It usually takes 3-5 business days if approvals go quickly. If you can't do peering we can use outbound-only with NAT which is lower friction.
04:08 Jordan Meyers: Let's talk timeline — Samira, what do you think is realistic for a pilot start?
04:12 Samira Gupta: If Pegasus can provide the sample prompts and grant network access within one week, we can start provisioning dev Dedicated resources and have a smoke test in ~2 weeks. So pilot start mid-December seems plausible.
04:26 Dana Ortiz: Mid-December is tight for us — two blockers: security review and sample data prep. We'll aim to have samples by Dec 6 and security sign-off by Dec 10.
04:38 Maya Lin: I can commit to an initial compliance doc review by Dec 4, if Jordan sends the SOC2 and SAML docs today.
04:45 Jordan Meyers: Will do — I have the links, will include runbook and network diagram.
05:00 Ethan Park: On benchmarking, we want a targeted test: 2k requests per second short-turn chat and a 25-token average. Can Redwood run a stress test against Dedicated?
05:12 Luca Romano: We can run internal perf tests and provide results; for accurate numbers we prefer a joint benchmark using your workload because token distribution matters. We can set up a benchmark harness and run with you.
05:26 Dana Ortiz: Great. Also curious about cost controls — can we set token caps and alerts?
05:34 Samira Gupta: Yes, the Console supports per-route quotas, token alarms, and cost dashboards. We'll recommend sensible defaults for pilot traffic.
05:46 Alex Chen: Any gotchas for model version pinning during rollouts? We need rollback paths.
05:53 Luca Romano: You can pin versions and do canary rollouts with automatic fallback policies. We'll add the recommended rollout strategy to the ops playbook.
06:08 Maya Lin: Small note — we operate in EMEA, data residency might be a requirement long-term. Does Redwood offer region-specific deployments?
06:15 Jordan Meyers: Yes, we have region options and can deploy Private control planes in specific cloud regions for enterprise customers. Mostly an enterprise feature.
06:22 Dana Ortiz: Ok, let's recap next steps. Jordan?
06:26 Jordan Meyers: I'll send the runbook, SOC2, SAML guide, KMS notes, and a link to the onboarding checklist after the call. Luca will provide dev endpoints once provisioned. Samira will draft the pilot success criteria. Pegasus to share sample prompts and QPS targets.
06:44 Ethan Park: One more question — we use a homegrown feature store, would Redwood need access to that or just precomputed embeddings?
06:51 Luca Romano: For inference we just need the inputs; if you want server-side embedding generation and storage, we can talk about embedding endpoints. But typically teams send precomputed embeddings or call embedding API as part of pipeline.
07:06 Dana Ortiz: Perfect. Anything else?
07:09 Maya Lin: Just to reiterate security: please include contact for incident response and details on data deletion procedures.
07:15 Samira Gupta: We'll include the IR contact and playbook.
07:22 Jordan Meyers: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with all artifacts and proposed calendar invites for deep-dive and perf bench.
07:30 Dana Ortiz: Thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript.
